'''Los Angeles International Airport'''{{Ref|(Note)}} was a pre-[[Great War|War]] [[airport]] located in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] which appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Background==
The airport survived the Great War mostly intact and is still a monumental landmark in the desert wastelands of California as of [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]]. Many [[aircraft]] crashed around the airport and its surrounding terrain during the Great War. Airplane parts have also been scavenged and/or salvaged for settlements such as [[Filly]]. At some point, a [[Soviet satellite|satellite]] owned by the [[Soviet Union]] also crashed near the airport. There was a [[donut shop]] located along a road not far from the airport.

In 2296, [[Lucy MacLean]] and [[Siggi Wilzig]] passed by the airport after escaping from Filly, en route to deliver Wilzig to [[Lee Moldaver]] at [[Griffith Observatory]]. Wilzig ultimately died nearby at the crashed Soviet satellite. Others tracking Wilzig (first [[the Ghoul]] and Wilzig's former dog [[CX404]], then [[Maximus]] and [[Thaddeus]] of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]]) would also pass by the area later.

==Notes==
* The airport is also prominently shown in the ending credits of "[[The Target]]," which depicts it as housing a fleet of [[Vertibird]]s, with numerous crashed and/or grounded airplanes shown around, as well as a billboard advertising [[Horizon Airlines]]. Two corpses in power armor are also seen, along with a poster of Uncle Sam modified to advertise the Brotherhood of Steel.

==Appearances==
The Los Angeles airport appears only {{in|FOTV}}, in the episodes "[[The Target]]" and "[[The Head]]." It also appears in a pre-War flashback in the episode "[[The Innovator]]."

==Behind the scenes==
* [[wikipedia:Los Angeles International Airport|Los Angeles International Airport]] is a real-world airport in Los Angeles, California. The large arch-like building in the middle of the airport is based on the real-world [[wikipedia:Theme Building|Theme Building]], built at the airport between 1957 and 1961.
** {{Note|(Note)}} No name has been given for this location in-universe, other than the audio narration for the ending credits of "[[The Target]]" identifying it as an airport, although it has been called LAX in news articles.<ref name="indiewire">[https://archive.ph/NeZIR ''Indiewire'': "'Fallout' Builds a World Unlike Any Other — Including the Video Game"]: ''"Los Angeles touchstones like the Capitol Records building, LAX, and Randy's Donuts were created digitally to anchor the viewer in the city."''</ref><ref>[https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/awards/story/2024-06-11/fallout-production-design-uses-new-york-coastal-africa ''Los Angeles Times'': "In 'Fallout,' a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from... Namibia?"]: ''"Worth's team provided the broken-arch remains of LAX's Theme Building with a giant, eaten-away Randy's Donuts nearby for the show's lead wanderers — Lucy, walking nightmare the Ghoul (Walton Goggins) and Maximus (Aaron Moten), a renegade from the fascistic Brotherhood of Steel — to pass by from various distances and directions."''</ref> The airport's real-world name is therefore used for this article.
* The airport was filmed entirely using digital effects.<ref name="indiewire" />

Wilds.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type =landmark |image =FOTV The Wilds Panorama.png |part of =[[New California]] |factions =[[Brotherhood of Steel]] (2296) |creatures =[[Yao guai (TV series)|Yao guai]] }} The '''Wilds''' are a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== The region known as the "Wilds" is shown to be a vast stretch of [[New California]] which includes some pre-[[Great War|War]] cityscapes of [[Los Angeles]] that have been retaken by nature, distinguished by its dense woods punctuated by overgrown urban structures, home to populations of wildlife including hostile mutated types such as [[Gulper (TV series)|gulpers]] and [[Yao guai (TV series)|yao guai]]. ==In the TV series== In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], after escaping initial capture during his defection from the [[Enclave]] and subsequent flight from their [[Enclave research colony|mountainous research colony]], [[Siggi Wilzig]] and his canine companion [[CX404]] pass through the Wilds on a trek to reach the trading town of [[Filly]]. They eventually come to a clearing outside a cave where Wilzig tries to consume a trail ration of [[Cram]] but is interrupted by his dog returning with a severed human hand and subsequently run off by nearby danger.Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} Wilzig's escape was later discovered by the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel]], who gave orders to a Brotherhood chapter called the [[Knights of San Fernando]], assigning them the mission of capturing Wilzig and his [[cold fusion|artifact]]. On the order of the San Fernando chapter's leader, [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]], several teams of [[Knight (TV series)|knights]] and their [[Brotherhood of Steel ranks#Squire|squires]] were sent to scour the Wilds in search of the Enclave defector.[[Quintus]]: "''Our mission comes from the highest clerics in the Commonwealth. It is believed that a denizen of the Enclave has escaped.''"
Squire: "''The Enclave's real?''"
Quintus: "''And that he has with him an object of profound potential to harm our nation or to save it. Each knight in this legion will search a section of the Wilds for this target. Brothers, we exist for moments such as these. Go forth with honor! And may the shape of the future be cut by your sword!''"
({{FOTV|1|1}}) One such team, composed of [[Titus|Knight Titus]] and his squire [[Maximus]] (replacing the original pick [[Dane (TV series)|Dane]]) disembarks from their vertibird in the section of the Wilds that Wilzig passed through. After coming across the scientist's campsite, the two investigate the cave suspecting that their target had been attacked and killed by its inhabitant. Subsequently, Titus is ambushed by the nesting yao guai, disarmed of his [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]], and attempts to flee in terror but is chased down and lethally mauled by the creature. After killing the yao guai, before Maximus could administer life-saving first aid with a [[Stimpak (TV series)|stimpak]], Titus' threats and hostile behavior cause him to withhold and insult the knight in return, calling him a disgrace to the Brotherhood and the [[:File:Shady Sands Knight and Maximus.png|knight]] that Maximus idolizes. With his squire withholding medical care, Titus expires from his wounds, after which Maximus takes his armor and disguises himself as Titus to continue the mission on his own and prove his worth to the Brotherhood. ==Appearances== The Wilds appear only {{in|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "The End" and "The Target." ==Behind the scenes== The establishing shot of the Wilds (used for the page) includes a foreground that is strikingly similar to [https://www.flickr.com/photos/cmdrcord/37481289074 Pripyat's Lenin Square], including the square itself, Palace of Culture Energetik, and the Polissya Pripyat hotel, though there is no supplementary evidence to date that it was used for a filming location. ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:New California]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

The '''Sunset Sarsaparilla factory''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

==Background==
The factory was constructed by the [[Sunset Sarsaparilla Company]] on a hilltop elevated above and overlooking the city of [[New Vegas|Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]] and was neighbored by a motel business. What is shown of the present-day area indicates it survived the [[Great War]] intact with little, if any [[radiation]] affecting it.

At some point, a [[RobCo Industries|RobCo]] [[Securitron]] ended up at the factory for unknown reasons. By 2296, a combination of age and lack of maintenance resulted in its programming going haywire, causing it to erratically shift between thinking it was a masseuse and a security guard.

==In the TV series==
===[[The Profligate]]===
Sometime after escaping from the [[KPSS radio station]] near [[Hollywood Hills]],<ref>{{FOTV|1|7}}</ref> the [[Mutations|mutated]] ex-[[Knights of San Fernando|Brotherhood]] squire [[Thaddeus]] left [[New California]] and made his way to the [[Mojave Wasteland]] where he discovered the abandoned factory. His exploration included finding its [[Extremely broken Securitron|malfunctioning "security guard"]] which he chose to stay apart from but still keep around for protection. With his access to the bottling floor, Thaddeus decided to set up a [[Bottle cap|cap]] collecting operation; to maximize profit, he installed himself as floor manager and gathered a "crew" of orphaned [[human]] and [[ghoul]] children to man the conveyor belts bringing out crates of soda so they could pry off the caps while drinking the leftover soda for refreshment.

The quiet living Thaddeus was enjoying was eventually upended when the bottling factory was stormed by [[Maximus]] and [[Xander Harkness]] from the [[Brotherhood of Steel (Fallout 4)|Commonwealth Brotherhood]] after they detected the plant's power signature. They destroyed the Securitron and discovered the crew of children, which Xander wanted to eliminate the ghouls in accordance with the [[Codex]]. Thaddeus tried to intervene to protect them, but Xander's refusal to back down forced Maximus to kill him by driving a [[Super sledge (TV series)|super sledge]] into his head.

===[[The Demon in the Snow]]===
Shortly after killing Xander, Maximus tells Thaddeus he has to help him cover it up from the Brotherhood, right as a vertibird arrives that was tracking them. Despite initial reluctance and claiming he prefers to run away, Thaddeus agrees to help after Max points out the Brotherhood would discover the kids in the process of looking for him, killing the ghouls and recruiting the humans, if they did not create a distraction. Thaddeus takes Maximus's suit of T-60 power armor and disguises himself as the Commonwealth paladin as they are flown back to [[Area 51]].

==Notes==
It is never explicitly clarified if this location is meant to be the [[Sunset Sarsaparilla headquarters]] that appeared in ''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]''. Although they both have large statues depicting a [[Sunset Sarsaparilla]] bottle in the front of their buildings, the two locations have more differences than they do similarities. The TV series location appears to more closely resemble a factory or warehouse in its exterior, differing greatly from the headquarters building which was largely an office structure with an attached factory. The interior layout of the headquarters also appears to differ considerably from what is visible in the TV series location. The area surrounding the factory in the TV series has several differences as well, having more space outside the building, and being located in close proximity to a motel and hills, far away from the city of [[New Vegas]], whereas the headquarters in ''Fallout: New Vegas'' is situated within the edges of the western part of the city.

==Appearances==
The Sunset Sarsaparilla factory appears only in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]].

The '''Fabulous New Vegas sign''' is an [[Fallout: New Vegas locations#Unmarked individual locations|unmarked location]] in the [[Mojave Wasteland]] {{In|FNV}}. It also appears {{in|FOTV}}.

==Layout==
The location is situated north of the main entrance to [[Camp McCarran]], close to the southern wall of the [[New Vegas Strip|Strip]].

==Notes==
* As suggested by its appearance in the [[Fallout: New Vegas intro|cinematic intro]] in which an [[NCR Veteran Ranger]] with an [[Anti-materiel rifle (Fallout: New Vegas)|anti-materiel rifle]] snipes a [[Fiends|Fiend]] by the [[El Rey Motel]], the sign does have a platform on the rear face of it. However, this platform is inaccessible to the player character by normal means, nor does any NPC ever use it as in the intro.
* In ''Fallout: New Vegas'', the sign was altered so that "New" covers the former name "Las" as well as the "e" in "New" actually being a number "3" reversed. There is also a smiley face painted in the "o" in "Welcome."

==Appearances==
The Fabulous New Vegas sign appears {{In|FNV}}, in the [[Fallout 4 holotape games|Pip-Boy minigame]] ''[[Atomic Command (Fallout 4)|Atomic Command]]'' {{In|FO4}} and {{in|FOTV}}.

==Behind the scenes==
* The in-game Fabulous New Vegas sign is based on the real-world [[Wikipedia:Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign|Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign]], which is located in [[wikipedia:Paradise, Nevada|Paradise, Nevada]].
* A physical recreation of the ''Fabulous New Vegas'' version of the sign was displayed at gaming conventions to promote ''Fallout: New Vegas''{{'}}s release in 2010.
* In the ''Fallout'' TV series, the sign first appeared in the credits for the [[Fallout TV series season 1|season 1]] episode "[[The Beginning]]." Prior to the release of [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]], a poster was released depicting the main characters underneath the sign.
** There are some slight differences with the sign in the TV series compared to how it appears in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. At the bottom of the sign, there is a sliver of plastic remaining from the pre-War sign that is not present in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. It features the logo and name of the real-world company [[wikipedia:YESCO|YESCO]], which owns and maintains the sign in real life. The text for "NEVADA" is white in ''Fallout: New Vegas'', but in the show, it has been darkened to more closely resemble its dark blue appearance in real life. Additionally, the end of the "D" is visible in ''Fallout: New Vegas'', but it is not visible on the poster, having been further worn away. In contrast to its ''Fallout: New Vegas'' appearance, the red star at the top of the sign in the TV series' current depiction is undamaged.

By the late [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2290s]], the sole occupant of KPSS is the radio host [[Carl (TV series)|Carl]], who fills the airtime entirely with a large collection of vintage fiddle music. Carl does not take visitors at the station, with an array of defensive traps, including massive bear traps and makeshift crossbows linked to tripwires, surrounding the main building to ensure anyone looking to place a request or make a complaint about his choice of music would sooner have an arrow lodged in their vital parts.[[Carl (TV series)|DJ Carl]] (via radio): ''"Hey-yo, this Is DJ Carl at KPSS, broadcasting from the base of the once-beautiful Hollywood Hills. So, I'd encourage you to sit back and enjoy the folksy, gutsy sound of bygone fiddlers. And, if you don't like what you hear, just a reminder that I don't take visitors to the station. A simple postcard will suffice. That said, enjoy the fiddling."''
{{FOTV|1|7}} The station exterior is littered with the displayed heads of those Carl refers to as his "[[critic]]s."[[Thaddeus]]: ''"Great job on these booby traps, by the way. Really good."''

'''Ma June's Sundries''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}.

==Background==
Owned and operated by the namesake [[Ma June]] for some time prior to [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], the general goods store serves as a mainstay of the trading town of [[Filly]] in [[New California]]. In addition to various bits and bobs including old [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] products and merchandise, June also keeps a selection of weapons behind the store counter for sale including [[Plasma pistol (TV series)|plasma pistols]], a [[Junk Jet (TV series)|Junk Jet]], [[Laser musket (TV series)|laser muskets]], etc. Due to the collapse of the [[New California Republic]]'s economy around the greater [[Los Angeles]] area following the destruction of [[Shady Sands]] in 2283, stores like Ma June's returned to the tried-and-true barter system utilizing [[bottle cap]]s with a prohibition on refunds.<ref>As seen in the {{FOTV|1|2}}</ref>

==''Fallout'' TV series==
===[[The Target]]===
[[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] enters Ma June's Sundries and, at first, comments about how Ma June was selling Vault-Tec items and surmises that she must do business with criminals. Aside from Lucy's interest in a [[Lee Moldaver|particular criminal]], Ma June was more interested in the fact that Lucy was a [[Vault]] dweller and tried to call on her roommate [[Barv]]. As Lucy tries to ask Ma June about the criminal she is looking for, while Ma June beckons Barv, Lucy alerts Ma June when she drops Moldaver's name.

After closing [[Ma June's ledger|her ledger]] and telling Barv to return to her room, Ma June then debates Lucy about her Vault naivete, who begs Ma June for any information on Moldaver. In the end, Ma June kicks Lucy out of her store, but as Lucy leaves, she runs into [[Siggi Wilzig]], who she met at her campfire the other night in front of the store.

The two would briefly talk until Ma June walked out of her store. After confirming Wilzig's identity, she told him to enter her store and demanded that Lucy scram. However, [[the Ghoul]], who sat on a chair close by to the store, accosts Wilzig, blows off his left foot, and in retaliation, Ma June puts a bounty on the Ghoul's head.

During the shootout between the Ghoul and the [[Filly townsperson|Filly townsfolk]] hoping to cash in on the bounty on the Ghoul's head. Lucy looked at Ma June's finance book and saw that Lee Moldavor's name was written in the book. She then confronts the Ghoul in front of the store and attempts to reason with him until [[Maximus]] appears inside a [[T-60 power armor]]. As Maximus distracted the Ghoul by fighting him, Lucy and Ma June carried Wilzig into the store's backroom, where Ma June demanded that Barv fetch a new leg. Though Barv complains that she was trying to eat her [[Pork n' Beans#Greasy Prospector Pork n' Beans|beans]], she still agrees to do it.

As Ma June tries to get Wilzig comfortable on a chair with his leg up on the table, Barv eventually arrives with a [[Jim's Limbs]] crate, and Ma June uses one of them on his blown-off foot. Once it was agreed that Lucy would transport Wilzig to Moldaver and Ma June input Moldaver's coordinates into her [[Pip-Boy]], the two left through the back door.

Afterward, the Ghoul entered Ma June's Sundries, where he spots a puddle of blood and a box of Jim's Limbs. Walking outside, the Ghoul finds the wounded CX404; he then takes CX404 into Ma June's Sundries and uses a [[Stimpak (TV series)|stimpak]] on her, which revives her.

===[[The Beginning]]===
It is unknown if Ma June returned to her shop and continued business following the Ghoul's massacre. By a later point in 2296, the town of Filly is taken over by the [[Brotherhood of Steel]], with the store in particular converted into an armory stockpiling their weaponry.

[[Cadillac Bob]] (writer; formerly) }} '''California Crest Studios''' was a pre-War [[Pre-War companies|motion picture company]] located in the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[California]]. Its main studio lot appears as a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== California Crest Studios was founded before the [[Great War]] and operated primarily in the [[Hollywood]] district of Los Angeles. Its main studio is located not far from a section of the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].At the beginning of "[[The Ghouls]]", [[Lucy MacLean|Lucy]] and [[the Ghoul]] are shown walking along a section of the Hollywood Walk of Fame, then at the end of "[[The Head]]," they pass by the ruins of California Crest Studios, indicating the two locations are within walking distance of each other. The company was well-known as the makers of the highly successful Western movie ''[[The Man from Deadhorse]]'' starring [[Cooper Howard]], and had already begun working on a sequel to the film around January 2077.[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]] news ticker: ''NO ONE'S BEATING THIS DEADHORSE. "THE MAN FROM DEADHORSE" TOPS BOX OFFICE. A SEQUEL IS ALREADY IN THE WORKS AT CALIFORNIA CREST STUDIOS.'' As of that month, they had also signed a deal with the [[Nuka-Cola Corporation]] for a seventeen-film series featuring the Nuka-Cola mascots [[Bottle]] and [[Cappy]].[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]] news ticker: ''NUKA-COLA MASCOTS 'BOTTLE AND CAPPY' TO APPEAR IN ANIMATED FILM FROM CALIFORNIA CREST STUDIOS. WILL BE THE FIRST IN A SEVENTEEN PICTURE DEAL BETWEEN THE COMPANIES.'' The studio worked with film services businesses such as catering company [[Catering to the Stars!]] and transportation and equipmental rental firm [[Studio Services]], and also operated a bus tour service, California Crest Studio Tours, for tourists visiting its physical location. The company was also known to utilize [[Mister Handy (TV series)|Mister Handy]] robotic units in their operations. Like much of the greater Los Angeles area, the bombs dropping reduced the studio building to rubble, with the desert winds and rolling sands of the [[wasteland]] gradually swallowing it up over the years. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Head]]=== In the first of two flashbacks to Cooper's life in the pre-War era, he is filming the final scene of his movie ''The Man from Deadhorse'' at the studio but cuts near the end and expresses his discomfort to the film's director [[Emil Dale]] about how his sheriff character is scripted to shoot and kill the outlaw played by his co-star [[Jorge]] rather than arresting him alive as always happens in his Western films. When Emil fails to convince him of the creative choices behind the decision, Cooper wants to involve one of the writers [[Cadillac Bob]] but is informed about the man's firing due to supposedly holding [[Communism|communist]] beliefs. Cooper's conversation with Emil is cut short when he sees his wife [[Barb Howard|Barb]] nearby. The loving partners share a touching moment when she tricks him into eating lavender taffy which he hates, before Barb hands him a package containing a [[Vault jumpsuit]] to wear for his promotional shoot in collaboration with Barb's employer, the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]]. Cooper reluctantly agrees, then opts to race their daughter [[Janey Howard|Janey]] to his trailer. In the present of [[Timeline#2296|2296]], [[the Ghoul]] and a captive [[Lucy MacLean]] march onto the site of the ruined California Crest Studios lot during the trek from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to a [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] near [[Santa Monica Boulevard]]. The bounty hunter stops at one point to survey the ruins, remembering the times long ago when he worked there as an actor. Lucy tries to beg for some nourishing water, but the Ghoul cruelly dumps the rest of his canteen onto the ground and then mockingly suggests she try drinking from a nearby irradiated pond. As they near the lot of the old studios, Lucy sees a pre-War billboard with [[Vault Boy]] on it right before the Ghoul shoots a hole through the mascot's face in quiet anger and they carry on.Events of {{FOTV|1|3}} In the second flashback, Cooper emerges from his trailer on the CCS lot dressed up in his jumpsuit, which Barb reveals she personally designed to incorporate the signature blue-and-gold color scheme of his sheriff character. Cooper then walks with his family through the backlot to the site of the promo shoot. There, Barb introduces him to Vault-Tec reps [[George Yaffe]] and [[Sarah Clements]]. Though they initially share banter, the reps fall awkwardly silent after Cooper asks if the jumpsuits are really [[radiation]]-proof, then hastily answer positively. As the shoot is getting ready to start, Cooper makes an off-hand suggestion to add a thumbs-up gesture, an idea the Vault-Tec employees applaud. ==Layout== What is shown of the company's assets in the TV series indicates that California Crest Studios consisted of a large number of hangars used for filming, with roads in between where props, actors' trailers, and other services could be located for shooting. The studios also had a large, two-story blue house with a large bronze statue of a woman holding a wireframe globe outside it. By 2296 long after the nuclear apocalypse, there is almost no trace left of the area except for the ruins of the house and the destroyed statue, along with some other smaller ruined houses some distance away from the area. ==Appearances== California Crest Studios appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]] "[[The Head]]" and was first mentioned in ''[[Fallout - A Special LIVE Report from Galaxy News]]'', a promotional video for the TV series. ==Behind the scenes== The post-War ruins of the California Crest Studios lot were filmed at the casino of [[wikipedia:Elizabeth Bay|Elizabeth Bay, Namibia]], a ghost town and former diamond mine. Other areas of the town were used to film various other scenes, such as the [[Santa Monica|Santa Monica Pier]] and abandoned houses shown in "[[The Target]]." ==Gallery== California Crest Studios.png|California Crest Studios backlot FOTV Roman actors.png|Romans FOTV California Crest Studios bus.png|Tour bus FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 1.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 2.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 3.png|Ruins FOTV California Crest Studios ruins 4.png|The Ghoul stares at the ruins ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox pre-War companies}} [[Category:California Crest Studios]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]]

{{For|an overview of appearances|Super Duper Mart}} {{Infobox location |games =FOTV |image =FOTV Super Duper Mart.png |part of =[[Santa Monica]], [[Los Angeles]] |factions =[[Govermint]] (benefactor) |owners =[[Super-Duper Mart (company)|Super-Duper Mart]] (pre-War)
[[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] (2296) }} The '''Super Duper Mart''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== One of many franchise locations across the [[United States of America|United States]] owned by the pre-[[Great War|War]] [[Super-Duper Mart (company)|Super-Duper Mart]] company, this particular store is located in [[Santa Monica]] in [[Los Angeles]] County, [[State#California|California]]. The bombs dropping in [[Timeline#2077|2077]] spared much of the building itself, though it was seemingly looted of much of its inventory by scavengers over the years. Sometime prior to [[Timeline#2296|2296]], the abandoned building was taken over by wastelanders [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]] and set up as a "legitimate" business selling medical supplies including [[inhaler vial]]s. To accrue a supply of the vials, they also entered into the market of organ-harvesting by hiring [[bounty hunter]]s to capture [[ghoul]] and human wastelanders alike, relying on a repurposed [[Mister Handy (TV series)|Mister Handy]] unit, [[Snip Snip]], to perform the crude surgical operations. At some point, [[Sorrel Booker]]'s [[Govermint]] secured Huey and Squirrel's operation under a protection racket, involving the occasional visit by Govermint "[[Sheriff (TV series)|sheriffs]]" to collect their cut of the profits while handling any troublemakers that could disrupt business. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Ghouls]]=== [[The Ghoul]] escorts a captive [[Lucy MacLean]] across the wasteland from [[Hollywood Boulevard]] to the Super Duper Mart in order to sell her to the organ-harvesters in exchange for a resupply of inhaler vials after losing them to the [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]]. Shortly after Lucy enters the fortified building, he collapses outside from withdrawal.Events of {{FOTV|1|4}} Lucy is greeted by Snip Snip in the supermarket lobby and led to Huey and Squirrel who send them to the medical room, meanwhile as she notices the several ghouls they have locked up. Lucy tries to plead her case but is astonished when the Mister Handy offers to restore her missing finger, previously cut off by the Ghoul. Lucy's relief to have not been sold into sex slavery is then squashed when Snip Snip reveals she is instead going to have her organs harvested, right before he tranquilizes her. After awakening on Snip Snip's operating table, Lucy manages to free herself before his buzzsaw can cut her too deep, then evades his attacks long enough to obtain and use an old defibrillator to fry his circuits. She then augments his tranq-gun arm and loads it with projectiles filled with [[Abraxodyne Chemical]] industrial cleaner to make acid darts. She brings the robot to the lounge and threatens Huey and Squirrel to release their captives. They initially comply and let out some of the ghouls, including [[Freed ghoul|one]] who thanks Lucy before leaving. When she notices another, [[Martha (TV series)|Martha]] still in her cell as well as some others, she demands their release, then fires a dart near the harvesters when they prove reluctant and try to warn her about the danger. Lucy finds out too late that the remaining ghouls she had released have turned feral. She quickly retreats as they charge forward, knocking over Snip Snip and attacking Huey and Squirrel. The two only manage to kill one before Squirrel is tackled and mauled by a second, followed by Huey taking down that one but failing to stop the third from tearing out his throat right before getting a mutual kill. As Lucy looks over the carnage, she finds Martha approaching her and starting to turn feral. Just as the ghoul gives in and attacks, Lucy arms herself with a [[10mm pistol (TV series)|10mm pistol]] and puts Martha down, to her own regret. The [[Vault 33]] dweller later emerges from the Super Duper Mart outfitted in a set of leather armor and discovers the incapacitated bounty hunter. Though she admits that she may end up becoming a mutant like him, she firmly states she will never become a cruel and heartless monster like him, providing a supply of inhaler vials before leaving. Rejuvenated, the Ghoul enters the ravaged supermarket and indulges in the harvesters' alcohol and drug supplies including taking more of the inhaler vials. He then discovers a holotape copy of ''[[The Man from Deadhorse]]'' and out of curiosity, plays it on the nearby [[Radiation King]] television set, becoming lost in memories of his former life as Cooper Howard in the era before the bombs. ===[[The Trap]]=== Sometime after Lucy's departure from the Super Duper Mart, the Ghoul is awoken by the arrival of men in sheriffs' uniforms who extract Snip Snip's fusion core and place him under arrest for allegedly disrupting a "legitimate" business protected by the "government." Under sheriff escort, the bounty hunter is taken from the Super Duper Mart to the [[BBQ Shack (TV series)|BBQ Shack]].Events of {{FOTV|1|6}} ==Layout== The Super Duper Mart in Santa Monica is located close to several ruined high-rises and is within walking distance of a massive impact crater left by a nuclear explosion. Potential transactions are directly made through an old speaker located outside the entrance. The building still has power by 2296, with working lighting displays and pre-War music being played on the speakers. The old commercial refrigerators in the store were repurposed as holding cells for captives waiting to have their organs harvested, with the locks controlled by a console operated by Huey and Squirrel, who typically reside in a lounge area in the center of the store where they mostly watched old holotapes on a TV and let Snip Snip handle most of the day to day work. A kids play area is also advertised within the store with small rides, and much of the store still retains the [[Halloween]] decorations that went up before the bombs. The Mister Handy primarily conducts his surgical operations in what appears to be the former store clinic. Despite the grisly outcome of his operations, Snip Snip still obeys some of his old healthcare programming and maintains a supply of medical equipment which he will use to mend injuries on wastelanders brought in, such as a drawer of multiple severed fingers to sew on in place of lost ones. The actual organ-harvesting takes places in a separate room repurposed as an operating theater. ==Appearances== The Santa Monica Super Duper Mart appears {{In|FOTV}} episodes "[[The Ghouls]]" and "[[The Trap]]." ==Behind the scenes== Scenes set in the Super Duper Mart were filmed around July to August 2022 at an empty ShopRite outlet redesigned with the fictional supermarket's signs and logo, located at 2424 Hylan Boulevard in Staten Island, New York. ==Gallery== FOTV Super Duper Mart crater.png|Across a crater in Los Angeles FOTV Super Duper Mart yard.png|The entrance yard of the building FOTV1-4 Daytripper.jpg|Bottles of [[Day Tripper|Daytripper]] seen on a countertop inside FOTV leaked set photo SDM July 2022.jpg|Leaked set photo from July 2022 ==References== {{References}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Super-Duper Mart locations]] [[ru:Супермаркет (телесериал)]] [[zh:大无敌超市(电视剧)]]

BROTHERHOOD BASE - DAY (102.20)"'' - [[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 29 ==History== ===Background=== A remote pre-[[Great War|War]] airport on the West Coast, the facility was taken over by the [[Knights of San Fernando]] chapter of the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] sometime before [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]].''"The middle of fucking nowhere. The remains of a hangar and runway tell us this place was once an airport."'' - [[The End script|"The End" script]], p. 30. It has since served a pivotal role in the Brotherhood's operations in and around [[New California]], acting as a training camp for the Brotherhood's countless aspirants. ===The End=== The area is introduced alongside the character of Maximus as other initiates are beating him by a set of bunker entrances before scattering. Many areas of the airbase are seen, including the runway, watchtower, barracks, and main hangars. Maximus is sentenced to latrine duty and exhibits extreme anger and frustration. Later during an engineering lesson in a hangar, the class is interrupted, with the aspirants running outside to see the arrival of [[The Prydwen|the ''Prydwen'']] and a squad of knights from the Eastern Brotherhood in T-60 armor. Maximus and Dane later sneak off to get an up-close look at one of the suits being stored in the garage. ===The Beginning=== {{Section|FOTV}} ==Layout== The base's layout includes extensive runways, hangars, barracks, and command facilities. Large swaths of tarmac allow Brotherhood [[Vertibird]]s to take off and land safely. A watchtower overlooks the runway and is also used by younger Brotherhood initiates to smoke. Initiates are seen clearing pathways, suggesting that the Brotherhood had recently taken the airbase, or are in the middle of restoring or expanding it. The base is also home to a large underground bunker complex, with at least nine separate partially submerged bunker entrances being visible adjacent to the airfield. Brotherhood of Steel members can be seen building what looks to be roadways between the bunkers and the rest of the base. By the 2290s, it was one of the Brotherhood's known strongholds on the West Coast. It is home to a sizable contingent of the organization's forces, including clerics, officers, support personnel, and a large number of aspirants of all ages. These aspirants and hopefuls are housed in the base's barracks section, which contains at least 23 barracks buildings and some medical tents. The buildings in the area appear to be built post-war, as fresh wood can be seen and there is no sign of dilapidated condition. From here, the recruits undergo training from [[clerics]] to become active field soldiers of the Brotherhood. The bunkhouses held both males and females together. Dane recovered in a tented clinic area close to the barracks after they were injured. One of the hangars was used by the clerics to teach classes on old-world technology for aspirants, utilizing desks and chalkboards. They punished wrong answers using a switch. A garage was used to store power armor suits at stations for the arriving Eastern Brotherhood knights. An old airplane was used as a meeting place between Elder Cleric Quintus and Maximus under the suspicion he had purposefully injured his friend Dane. Another building was used as an armory for all types of weapons. ==Notes== The pre-War [[Flag of the United States|American flag]] can be seen still being flown at the airbase, alongside the Brotherhood flag, despite the Brotherhood largely viewing the former USA as a failed nation in previous ''Fallout'' media. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:FNV Nellis AFB poster Keeping America Safe.png|thumb|right|x200px|"Keeping America Safe!"]] * The scenes for the Brotherhood airbase were filmed at [[wikipedia:Wendover Air Force Base|Wendover Airport]] in [[Utah]], formerly known as Wendover Air Force Base until 1969. The base prominently served as the training site of the [[wikipedia:509th Composite Group|509th Composite Group]], the B-29 unit that carried out the [[wikipedia:Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki|atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki]] during [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]]. The locations used for filming include: ** Ordnance storage area, where [[Maximus]] receives a beat-down from [[Thaddeus]] and his [[Thaddeus' minion|minions]]. The western part of the area is also used to depict latrine digging. ** The control tower, base headquarters, and operations building are next to hangar #1. ** Airmen dormitories are in the northeastern part of the base (with two tents set up in front of the dining hall, housing communications equipment, and the infirmary). ** Parked [[Vehicles in the Fallout TV series|C-123 and staff car]] next to the squadron hangar, in the scene where Maximus is interrogated by Cleric [[Quintus]]. ** The buildings at the western part of the ordnance storage area, currently used by the [https://clui.org/clui-locations/clui-wendover/points-interest-around-old-wendover-airfield/clui-wendover Center for Land Use Interpretation]. * The hangar at the airbase features a poster that heavily resembles the [[Nellis Air Force Base]] "Keeping America Safe!" [[Poster (Fallout: New Vegas)|poster]] from [[Fallout: New Vegas loading screens|loading screens]] {{In|FNV}}. The same text can be seen on the bottom of the poster, and text can also be seen on the top of the poster. {{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type = |image =FOTV Official Trailer Still 034.png |part of =[[Hollywood]], [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] |creatures =[[Gulper (TV series)|Gulper]]
[[Deer]]
[[Leech]] }} '''Hollywood Boulevard''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== In the era before the [[Great War]], Hollywood Boulevard was famous as a cultural icon of the [[Hollywood]] district of [[Los Angeles]], [[State#California|California]], running through many tourist areas. Museums, landmarks, and more defined its attraction. After the bombs struck, a large part of the boulevard located off of Exit 12A from a nearby highway became submerged and surrounded by overgrown forests, with the concrete skeletons of old, stripped buildings still popping out of the water; by [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], several have collapsed and sunk below the surface. A population of [[deer]] is present in the area, preyed upon by other creatures inhabiting the flooded areas, such as [[leech]]es. By 2296, the flooded area had become home to at least one [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]], mutant creatures originally created by [[radiation]] experiments in [[Vault 4]]'s Level 12 laboratory, some of which evidently managed to escape from the Vault at some point after the [[Great War]].As seen in {{FOTV|1|7}} ==In the TV series== ===[[The Head]]=== While carrying the decapitated head of [[Siggi Wilzig]] on her solo trek to find [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]], [[Lucy MacLean]] reaches the flooded shores of the Boulevard where she is briefly amazed by the peripheral view of the area, then spots a baby deer drinking by the lakeside. She tries to feed it some grass and admire the peaceful atmosphere until a gulper strikes fast from the lake, dragging the deer into the water from behind a thicket of tall grass and forcing Lucy to equip her [[Tranq gun (TV series)|tranq gun]].Events of {{FOTV|1|3}} The gulper reemerges and catches Lucy off-guard, using its tongue to latch onto her backpack trying to drag her into the water too. Lucy manages to stun it by firing a tranq dart into the gulper's mouth. However, as the creature retreats, it catches the cloth sack holding the head, tearing it away as it returns to the depths. Pursuing the creature to the opposite side of the boulevard, Lucy listens as her [[Pip-Boy 3000 Mark V|Pip-Boy]]'s [[geiger counter]] starts to go off at detecting the intense radiation in the water. She remembers the tracker she implanted into the head and uses her Pip-Boy to track its location and prepares to go after it. However, she is interrupted by the arrival of [[the Ghoul]] following [[CX404]] who tracked Wilzig's scent to the Boulevard. After striking Lucy with his [[Dom Pedro (TV series weapon)|revolver]], the bounty hunter demands to know where the head is. When Lucy does not answer, he ransacks her backpack but does not find it. Though Lucy tries to tell him that she lost the head, the Ghoul, upon examining a nearby pile of animal droppings, deduces that the creature that attacked her and took the head is a gulper. Taking Lucy prisoner, the Ghoul ties up the Vault dweller and secures her to an old shipyard winch with an attached anchor. Lucy attempts to plead and strike a deal with the Ghoul, but he ignores her and starts dunking her into the irradiated waters, causing her geiger counter to go off again. Lucy frustratedly questions why he is torturing her, but the Ghoul elaborates that he is not interested in torture, rather merely using her as bait to attract the gulper and retrieve the head, then drops her in one more time. Eventually, Lucy's struggling makes enough noise to lure over the gulper, which bites down on the winch anchor to drag her deeper. The Ghoul manages to work the winch's controls and pull Lucy back along with the gulper onto the dock. While the gulper is trying to eat Lucy, the Ghoul attacks it with a harpoon but is pushed back. After it clamps down on her leg, taking off her boot, Lucy grabs the Ghoul's satchel and throws it into the gulper's mouth as a distraction, along with CX404 landing a bite on one of its limbs. The gulper spits out the satchel and retreats into the water, taking the head with it. Once the Ghoul recovers, he inspects his satchel and discovers that the gulper managed to destroy the tin containing his supply of [[inhaler vial]]s. In anger, he takes Lucy prisoner again, tying a rope leash onto the Vault dweller in order to take her to trade for more vials at the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]]. Lucy again tries to beg with him, citing the Golden Rule, but the Ghoul callously replies that the wasteland has its own Golden Rule: "Thou shalt get sidetracked by bullshit every goddamn time." Lucy notices they are leaving CX404 behind at the waterside, but the Ghoul brushes it off stating the dog is not his. Sometime after Lucy and the Ghoul departed from the Boulevard, [[Thaddeus]] and [[Maximus]] (disguised as [[Titus|Knight Titus]]) arrive there following the radiation signature of the Ghoul, trying to locate the head themselves. When the tracker leads them into the waters of the flooded area, Thaddeus realizes the signature is not coming from the Ghoul but something else. The two then spot the gulper surfing through the water towards them. Maximus-as-Titus orders Thaddeus back to shore as he attempts to shoot the creature with his [[T60 pistol (TV series)|T60 pistol]] but to no effect. As the knight is confronted by the gulper emerging from the water, Thaddeus distracts it with a shot from a [[Heavy assault rifle (TV series)|heavy assault rifle]], but this causes it to charge toward him instead, managing to get his legs in its mouth. As the gulper tries to devour Thaddeus, Maximus runs after him and manages to stop the squire from being swallowed whole. Using the loose anchor caught in its mouth as a foothold, with a battlecry of "Ad victoriam!", Maximus extracts Thaddeus from the gulper's mouth and in the process pulls out a large portion of its innards, killing it. The two share a brief moment thanking the other for their help, then notice CX404 nearby licking at the head regurgitated by the gulper. Once they confirm it to be the object of their mission, they cheer in celebration and later depart from the Boulevard with their find. ==Behind the scenes== * The location of Hollywood Boulevard is based on the [[wikipedia:Hollywood Boulevard|real-world street of the same name]], which runs through Hollywood, Los Angeles. The highway exit marked on the Hollywood Boulevard road sign in the TV series, Exit 12A, is likewise a real-world freeway junction in Los Angeles, connecting Highway 101 with Lankershim Boulevard. ** A pre-release promotional image from the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|first season's Amazon overview page]] depicted the Hollywood Boulevard area from the TV series, but with the exit sign reading "Lankershim Boulevard" instead of Hollywood Boulevard. * Scenes taking place at Hollywood Boulevard was filmed at the [https://www.townofcortlandt.com/cn/webpage.cfm?tpid=18195 Cortlandt Quarry] in [[wikipedia:Verplanck, New York|Verplanck, New York]], situated at the northwesternmost lake within hamlet limits. Another location within Westchester County, Briarcliff Manor, was also used for scenes taking place at [[Hollywood Hills]] in the [[The End (episode)|first episode]].[https://archive.ph/Szq8p Visit Westchester County NY: Filmed in Westchester (archived)] ==Gallery== Fallout Season 1 Amazon CX404 bg.jpg|Pre-release promotional image from the [[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 Amazon overview page]], showing the sign's original design reading "Lankershim Boulevard" ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Roadways]]

It also appears in [[Fallout TV series season 2|season 2]] of {{in|FOTV|noin}}, as well as ''[[Fallout Shelter]]''. ==Background== A fixture along the route of [[Highway 95]] since before the [[Great War]], the Dino Dee-Lite catered to tourists and travelers, with [[Dinky the T-Rex]] serving as a roadside attraction.[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide faction profiles#Novac|''Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide'' faction profiles]], p. 43: ''"Watching over them is the landmark of the area: a giant fabricated tyrannosaurus rex biting off the top of "The World's 2nd Largest Thermometer". The interior of "Dinky" also serves as the city center (a converted gift shop from pre-war times, with a sniper's nest in Dinky's mouth). Dinky is the "attraction" that drew in tourists.''" After the nuclear apocalypse, the motel survived intact but sat vacant for years until the town of Novac was founded around it, taking its name from the broken motel sign by the entrance.[[Rose of Sharon Cassidy|Cass]]: ''"Named this place after the hotel. NoVac's the hotel, not the lizard.''"
([[RoseofSharonCassidy.txt|Cass' dialogue]]) By [[Timeline#2281|2281]], [[Jeannie May Crawford]] serves as the motel's proprietor and takes pride in Novac's small-town appeal. ==Layout== Situated in the center of Novac, the Dino Dee-lite complex has both a motel and gift shop. A courtyard is situated in the middle of the buildings, where [[Novac settler]]s can be found walking or sitting on the ground. The dinosaur houses the motel's [[Dino Bite gift shop|gift shop]] as well as a sniper nest in the dino's mouth.''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Manny Vargas' room: ''"The sniper in the mouth of Dinky the Dinosaur that watches over Novac during the day is Manny Vargas.''"''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Craig Boone's room: ''"The sniper in the mouth of Dinky that watches Novac at nighttime is Boone. This is his room, and if he’s in it, he tells you to get out, and meet him up in the mouth at 9 PM.''" The main building is the [[Dino Dee-lite front desk|front desk]], which contains the [[Mojave Express dropbox]] and serves as the office from which motel rooms are rented. Outside of the entrance to the front desk is the sign displaying the town's name.''[[Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition Tour of the Mojave Wasteland|''Fallout: New Vegas Official Game Guide Collector's Edition]]'' p. 410, Dino Dee-lite front desk: ''"Jeannie May Crawford heads up the front of house in the Motel, the broken sign of which is where the town takes its name. There are actually "Vacs" and for 100 Caps, you can lease a room right here, in the attached block, for as long as you like. Jeannie May is also a party of interest in Side Quest: One For My Baby. You can obtain a key to the floor safe behind the counter if you Pickpocket (or kill) her. There's a few other items in this room, too: Quest Item: Jeannie May's Safe Key, Cash Register Items, Quest Item: Dino Dee-Lite Room Key, Floor Safe Items [Easy], First Aid Box, Quest Item: Bill of Sale, Dinky the T-Rex Souvenir (5), Bottle Caps (150+) and Home Sweet Home.''" Next to the main building's entrance is a gate into a fenced-in area containing the motel rooms and bungalows. Several individuals live in the motel rooms, including [[Daisy Whitman]], [[Bruce Isaac]], [[Manny Vargas]], and [[Craig Boone]]. Two of the motel rooms are vacant, and entrance to the room as well as items found within are marked to owned. The second floor of the motel, from left to right while facing the building, contains the [[Dino Dee-lite motel room|player home]], a vacant room with a twin bed, [[Bruce Isaac's room]], and [[Daisy Whitman's room]]. The first floor, in the same fashion, has [[Manny Vargas' room]], a vacant room with a queen-sized bed, and [[Boone's room]]. All other rooms are boarded up and inaccessible. One can rent one of the motel rooms from Jeannie May for 100 [[Bottle cap (Fallout: New Vegas)|caps]]; alternatively, if one has an ''Accepted'' or higher [[Fallout: New Vegas reputations#Novac|reputation]] with Novac, she will give it to them for free. If Jeannie May is killed (either independently or as part of [[One for My Baby]]), then [[Cliff Briscoe]] will give them the room key. ==Notes== * While the Dino Dee-lite Motel has windows along its back wall (which [[No-bark Noonan]] will sometimes peer into), none of the motel rooms have corresponding windows on the inside. * In the TV series, there is an empty swimming pool in the courtyard between the motel and Dinky that does not exist in ''Fallout: New Vegas''. This swimming pool is also present in the version of Novac that appears in ''Fallout Shelter''. ==Appearances== The Dino Dee-lite Motel appears {{In|FNV}}, {{in|FOTV|noin}}, and {{in|FOS|noin}}. It is also mentioned {{in|FO76}}.{{Atom}} [[Plushie|Dinky Plushie]] [[Atomic Shop]] entitlement description: ''"The tag reads 'Dino Dee-lite Motel', sounds nice!"'' ==Behind the scenes== For the TV series, the Dino Dee-lite Motel was filmed at the abandoned Royal Hawaiian Motel in Baker, California. The motel was demolished in 2025, not long after filming ended.[https://archive.ph/YipBB r/fotv post: "Filming location for season 2, taken from Fallout New Vegas"] ==Gallery== ===''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]''=== FNV Novac motel front view.png|Outline of specific rooms DDL_Motel_room.jpg|An overview of all the rooms FNV_Novac_motel_backside.jpg|Back of motel view DinoDeeLitePropertyOverview01.png|Another view FNV Novac sign close up.jpg|Front sign close up ===[[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]]=== Novac Courtyard FOTV Season 2.png|An aerial view of the courtyard FOTV Great Khans Novac.png|[[Great Khans]] hanging [[The Ghoul]] on a noose built from the swimming pool's diving board ===''[[Fallout Shelter]]''=== FOS Novac.jpg ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox locations FNV}} {{Navbox Novac}} [[Category:Novac buildings]] [[Category:Hotels]] [[Category:Post-War businesses]] [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Fallout Shelter locations]] [[de:Dino-Dee-Lite-Motel]] [[es:Recepción del Dino Dee-Lite]] [[ru:Мотель «Дино дилайт»]] [[uk:Мотель «Діно Ділайт»]] [[zh:欢乐恐龙汽车旅馆]]

{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |mentions =FO1, FORPG |type = |image =FTV S2E2 Still 209.png |image desc =Area 51 after the Great War |part of =[[State#Nevada|Nevada]] |owners =[[United States Air Force]] (pre-War)
[[Brotherhood of Steel]] (2296) |map marker = }} {{Quotation|Property of Area 51, return if found|Written on the [[Alien Ship]]}} '''Area 51''' is a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{In|FOTV}}. ==Background== Pre-[[Great War|War]], Area 51 was a military garrison for the [[United States Air Force]]. It housed research facilities studying captured [[alien]] technology, including a [[flying saucer]]. The vessel was later retaken by its alien crew, but ended up crashing somewhere within [[State#California|California]] where it remained well into the 23rd century by 2161.[[PRO SCEN.MSG (Fallout)]]: ''"{40000}{}{Dome}"''
''"{40001}{}{You find a small label that reads: 'Property of Area-51. Return if found.'}"'' By late 2077, other artifacts stored in its warehouses included a preserved [[Zetan|Zetan corpse]], various pieces of alien technology including a [[shock baton]], [[Alien blaster (Fallout 3)|alien blaster]], and [[UFO]], a copy of the [[Constitution of the United States]], an artifact resembling the Ark of the Covenant, a [[Terracotta Army]] soldier, and a [[Holy Hand Grenade]]. The facility's location within the deserts of the West Coast inspired military engineers to create an array of wind turbines around its perimeter, powered by a fusion generator, that could rapidly clear away large sand deposits in minutes (similar to the [[DERVISH camouflage system]] utilized by the [[Hidden Valley bunker|bunkers]] of [[Hidden Valley]]). When not in use, the turbines themselves are housed within underground silos to preserve them. After the nuclear apocalypse, a number of [[Zetan]] aliens that had been held captive within the facility escaped and retreated to [[Skull Canyon]].''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]]'' scenario ''[[Showdown in Skull Canyon]]'', pp. 4, 16. At some point, the rolling sands and desert winds of the [[wasteland]] buried much of the pre-War structures under an immense layer of sand, but the power control tower for the wind turbine array (housed in a fake playground rocket structure) was left exposed and accessible. ==In the TV series== ===[[The Golden Rule]]=== Sometime after the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory]] in [[Timeline#2296|2296]], the [[Knights of San Fernando]] uncovered the location of Area 51 and decided on claiming it as their new headquarters. After [[Maximus]] and his squad of knights obtained a pre-War holodisk which [[Quintus|Elder Cleric Quintus]] called the "key" to Area 51, a sizable number of the San Fernando chapter traveled to the pre-War military base on board the ''[[Caswennan]]''. On-site at the fake playground structure, a pair of scribes used a [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]] to power the ground console, in conjunction with another scribe who plugged in the key to a console on the ''Caswennan''{{'}}s flight deck, to reactivate the wind turbines and clear away the years of sand built-up that managed to keep much of Area 51 preserved. After exploring the central warehouse and recovering a substantial number of pre-War artifacts and weaponry, Area 51 became the new base of the chapter. It later served as the site of Quintus' meeting with the other elders of the [[Grand Canyon Brotherhood of Steel|Grand Canyon]], [[Coronado Brotherhood of Steel|Coronado]], and [[Yosemite Brotherhood of Steel|Yosemite]] chapters to begin planning for a civil war with the [[Commonwealth Brotherhood of Steel|Commonwealth Brotherhood]] with the intent of shifting the axis of power within the wider Brotherhood back to the West Coast.{{FOTV|2|2}} ===[[The Profligate]]=== {{Section|FOTV}} ==Appearances== [[File:FO1AlienSaucer.png|thumb|The [[Alien Ship]], a special encounter in ''[[Fallout]]'']] Area 51 appears only {{In|FOTV}} [[Fallout TV series episodes|episode]]s "[[The Golden Rule]]" and "[[The Profligate]]." It is mentioned in ''[[Fallout]]'', as a print on a flying saucer in the [[Alien Ship]] [[Fallout special encounters|special encounter]]. It was intended to appear in ''[[Fallout 2]]'', inhabited by a group of scientists, but was [[Fallout 2 cut content|cut]] from the final version of the game.[[Fallout 2 Official Strategies & Secrets]], p. 335: ''"A second set of drafts hypothesized the army of the Master (from ''Fallout 1'') roaming the wastes in a huge, armored land fortress, scooping up muties to use as slave labor. As you can see, neither of these stories made their way into the final game. Although some parts of them did—Lynette's head, for example, was once going to be the spokesperson for a group of scientists living in the ruins of a base in Area 51."'' It is also mentioned in ''[[Showdown in Skull Canyon]]'', a scenario for ''[[Fallout: The Roleplaying Game]].'' ==Behind the scenes== * Area 51 is based on the real world Groom Lake Facility, code named [[wikipedia:Area 51|Area 51]]. It is located within the Nevada Test and Training Range. The base is used by the United States military to develop and test many top secret aircraft and weapons technology, though it has long been a source of speculation among conspiracy theorists. Many theories involve captured aliens and their technology, hence why the location is mentioned on a crashed alien ship in ''Fallout''. * In an early draft of ''Fallout 2'', [[Joanne Lynette]]'s talking head was supposed to be used for a spokesperson for a group of scientists living in the ruins of Area 51. However, this never made it into the game. * For ''Fallout 2'', [[Chris Avellone]] also entertained the possibility of an Area 51 location consisting of nothing but the set for a fake moon landing.[https://www.watchoutforfireballs.com/61e ''Watch Out for Fireballs!'', Extrasode: Fallout 2 (Part 2) - Feat. Chris Avellone] * Area 51 was never planned for inclusion in ''[[Fallout: New Vegas]]'' from the start.Question: ''Was Big MT made because you weren't able to use Area 51? I think I saw someone say before you couldn't use Area 51 because Bethesda wanted to use it.''
[[Joshua Sawyer]]: ''No. We never intended to use Area 51.''
([[Joshua Sawyer Formspring posts|Formspring reply on July 3, 2012]]) When asked why, [[Joshua Sawyer]] stated that the land between [[New Vegas]] and Area 51 was not close nor interesting enough for inclusion. In addition, he remarked on the popular culture association between the base and extraterrestrials, which had already been covered in the ''[[Fallout 3]]'' [[Fallout 3 add-ons|add-on]] ''[[Mothership Zeta (add-on)|Mothership Zeta]]''.'''Fallout: New Vegas is tied with Fallout 3 for my favorite game, but my question is why didnt you guys add Area 51 to the game world considering how close it is to the Air Force base? I'm hoping that it will be a DLC because you guys could do a great job.'''
[[Joshua Sawyer]]: ''It really isn't that close and there's not a lot going on in the land between Las Vegas and Area 51.
http://maps.google.com/maps?f=d&sou...6.410231,-115.427856&spn=2.157308,4.22699&z=9
Also, Area 51 is most closely associated with (in popular culture, anyway) aliens, a subject Bethesda dealt with in Mothership Zeta.''
([[Joshua Sawyer Formspring posts/2010]]) * Exterior scenes for the base were filmed at Dumont Dunes in California. The interior of the main hangar was filmed at Wendover Airfield in Utah, which had also been used for scenes set at the [[Brotherhood base]] in the [[Fallout TV series season 1|first season]]. ==Gallery== Area 51 FOTV s2 teaser.png FTV S2E2 Still 208.png FTV S2E3 Still 135.png FTV S2E4 Still 218.png FTV S2E4 Still 291.png FTV S2E2 Still 210.png FTV S2E2 Still 337.png ==References== {{References}} '''Non-game''' {{References|group="Non-game"}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} {{Navbox locations FO2}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[Category:Fallout mentioned-only locations]] [[Category:Fallout 2 cut locations]] [[Category:United States Armed Forces locations]] [[Category:Military and research facilities]] [[pl:Strefa 51]] [[pt:Area 51]] [[ru:Зона 51]] [[uk:Зона 51]] [[zh:51区]]

Vault 24.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |mentions = |type = |owners =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (formerly) |image =FTV S2E1 Still 151.png }} '''Vault 24''' is a [[Vault-Tec Corporation|Vault-Tec]] [[Vault]] located in the [[Mojave Wasteland]]. It appears as a [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}, while a jumpsuit from the Vault was [[Fallout: New Vegas cut content|cut]] from {{In|FNV|noin}}. ==Background== {{Quotation|Individual is secondary to the collective. (Mandarin) ...true comrade chooses cooperation over individualism. (Mandarin) Our enemy has chosen the interest of product over the interest of people. We choose people over product. Freedom is inevitable. (Mandarin) The revolution will not be futile. (Mandarin)|Fragment of a mixed English/Chinese holotape used to recondition Vault dwellers. The tape alternates between the two languages and loops.}} [[file:FTV S2E1 Still 180.png|right|220px|thumb|The Ghoul picks up an ushanka with a red star, the international symbol of communism.]] Vault 24 was [[Vault#True purpose|designed]] to preserve and continue research into mind-control technologies, with [[Vault-Tec]]'s experimental staff using Americans assigned to the Vault as test subjects once the protocol was initiated. While they experimented with a variety of surgical techniques and reconditioning, the most successful was the [[brain-computer interface chip]] or "black box":[[Hank MacLean]]: "''Looks like a couple of the Vault experiments ran into some speed bumps. 24 made progress on the brain-computer interface.''" American dwellers fitted with this device were successfully converted to [[communism]], replacing Vault-Tec and American iconography with the flags of China, communist propaganda, and eschewing [[Vault jumpsuit]]s in favor of simple two-piece red garments with a prominent red star on the left-hand side and an ushanka with another red star bordered in gold.{{FOTV|2|1}} The Vault eventually failed, although the reasons for the failure are unclear. By 2296, mummified corpses of Vault dwellers litter the halls, some found still gathered at tables during what might be a council or soviet meeting, others still strapped to gurneys and medical chairs in the research laboratories, once forcibly made to watch videos meant to recondition them, with electrodes implanted into their brains. Once his true nature was revealed by [[Lee Moldaver]], the escaped [[Hank MacLean]] made his way to Vault 24 to seize the Vault's treasure trove of research. Vault laboratory 7HSZMS380200313 and the Vault itself was abandoned by this time, and he successfully took the data drive with him. [[Lucy MacLean]] and the [[Ghoul]] subsequently tracked him to the Vault, finding evidence of the Vault experiment within, and an [[Sunburned man|unfortunate victim]] of Hank's, who was used as a test subject to verify the functionality of the black box and leave a message for his daughter in gruesome fashion. ==Layout== [[File:FTV S2E1 Still 176.png|right|240px|thumb|The overgrown entrance hall]] Vault 24 was hidden beneath a [[Starlight Drive-in Theatre (TV series)|Starlight Drive-in Theatre]], with the Vault door concealed behind the movie screen. Inside the rocky outcropping was an arched entrance hall with a centrally-placed elevator granting access to the lower levels of the Vault. Damage to the structure of the Vault following its failure allowed sunlight and moisture to enter, leading to limited vegetation growing over the infrastructure, although nowhere near to the extent of places like [[Vault 22]]. The lower levels followed standard Vault-Tec designs, with living quarters provided for all dwellers. The experiment and provided supplies have led reconditioned dwellers to redecorate the Vault using modified [[Chinese]] flags to signify their newfound allegiance. The areas remained functional by 2297, although only low-power lighting was available by the time Hank MacLean entered the Vault. Below the living quarters lay the two-floor research level,The upper floor and stairs leading to it are visible when Lucy approaches the terminal. stocked with scientific and medical equipment necessary to continue work on the black box and perform the surgeries necessary for advancing the development of the brain-computer interface allowing for controlling minds. ==Notes== * Vault 24's experiment bears similarity to the story of [[Camp Liberty]] in ''Fallout 76'', introduced in the ''[[Skyline Valley (update)|Skyline Valley]]'' [[Fallout 76 updates|update]]. Both Vault 24 and Camp Liberty used brainwashing techniques to turn their residents into adherents of communism, including through visual presentations that included hypnotic spiral imagery. Camp Liberty's experiment was part of [[Operation Sleeping Giant]], an initiative of the [[Defense Intelligence Agency]]. ==Appearances== Vault 24 appears in the ''Fallout'' TV series episode "[[The Innovator]]." ==Behind the scenes== {{FNVCC}} * A [[Vault jumpsuit (Fallout: New Vegas)#Vault 24 jumpsuit|Vault 24 jumpsuit]] was [[Fallout: New Vegas cut content|cut]] from ''Fallout: New Vegas''; it remains in the game files but can only be accessed with [[Fallout: New Vegas console commands|console commands]]. The Vault itself and any details regarding it cannot be found in the game. According to [[Joshua Sawyer]], the ''New Vegas'' developers did not make any concepts for Vault 24; the Vault itself was never intended to appear in-game, and its Vault jumpsuit may have been generated specifically for [[Sarah Weintraub]]'s unmarked quest [[Suits You, Sarah]].Question: '''I was reading up on New Vegas cut content and came across 'Vault 24', but apparently no plans or content beyond a jumpsuit exist for it in game files. Griffith Observatory.original_wikitext:
{{Infobox location |games =FOTV |type = |image =FOTV Griffith Observatory.png |image desc =Appearance {{In|FOTV}} |part of =[[Boneyard|Los Angeles]] |local map = |factions =[[New California Republic]] (2283 - 2296) |owners =[[Vault-Tec Corporation]] (pre-War) }} '''Griffith Observatory''' is a post-[[Great War|War]] settlement and [[Fallout TV series locations|location]] {{in|FOTV}}. ==Background== Prior to the [[Great War]], Griffith Observatory was sponsored by the [[Vault-Tec Corporation]] and designated as a "Science & Friendship Center."{{FOTV|1|7}}: Seen on a billboard in the credits sequence. The observatory was able to survive the devastation caused by the nuclear strikes on [[Los Angeles]], although it suffered some structural damage along with wear and tear over the following 200 years. Around [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2283|2283]], a nuclear bomb destroyed the [[New California Republic]] capital of [[Shady Sands]]. The NCR presence in Los Angeles subsequently declined; however, surviving NCR forces who were not in Shady Sands when it was destroyed coalesced under the leadership of [[Lee Moldaver]],[[Norm MacLean]]: ''"So you met my sister?"''
[[Ma June]]: ''"Yeah, back in Filly. Before the Brotherhood of Steel burnt it down. Had her help a fella from the Enclave get through the Shithole to some folks from the NCR who weren't in town when Shady Sands blew up. Pretty slim odds. What with it being Khan country."''
({{FOTV|2|5}}) a pre-War scientist and notable figure in Shady Sands prior to its destruction. She led them to garrison the old observatory, which became the last known remaining NCR headquarters in Los Angeles, housing both [[NCR citizen (TV series)|civilians]] and [[NCR soldier (TV series)|NCR soldiers]]. There, she hoped to restore the ruined Shady Sands' prospects by building a [[cold fusion]] reactor using technology she herself had created over 200 years ago. However, the reactor required two essential components: the first was a cold fusion diode, and the second were the credentials of a pre-War Vault-Tec employee. The credentials were needed to activate the reactor inside the observatory, as the cold fusion technology had become proprietary to Vault-Tec before the Great War. In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], Moldaver acted to obtain both components. She and her [[Moldaver's elite guard|elite guard]] led a gang of [[Vault 32 raider|raiders]] to infiltrate the [[Three Vaults]] under [[Santa Monica]], masquerading as residents of [[Vault 32]] to enter [[Vault 33]] during their Triennial Trade ceremony. In their subsequent attack, they were are able to capture 33's overseer [[Hank MacLean]] and escape with him as their prisoner after the raiders massacred many of the Vault dwellers, bringing him to the observatory.Events of {{FOTV|1|1}} The goal of this was to have Hank relinquish his Vault-Tec executive credentials in order to unlock the encryption on the cold fusion reactor. To obtain the cold fusion diode itself, Moldaver got in contact with [[Siggi Wilzig]], a member of the [[Enclave]] who had possession of it, and made arrangements for him to come to her at the observatory to deliver the technological artifact. In response to her father's abduction by Moldaver, [[Lucy MacLean]] set out into the wasteland to find and rescue him, later being given coordinates to the observatory from [[Ma June]], who had been paid to assist Wilzig's own arrival there. Interference by [[the Ghoul]] and Brotherhood of Steel ends up forcing Lucy to instead take the severed head of Wilzig containing the cold fusion artifact to trade for her father's life.Events of {{FOTV|1|2}} She was eventually able to arrive at the observatory, where she met Moldaver, who then obtained the diode from Lucy and the codes from Hank. However, the observatory was attacked by the [[Brotherhood of Steel]] chapter known as the [[Knights of San Fernando]] just before the reactor could be activated. In the [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|ensuing battle]], the NCR forces at the observatory were routed, with Moldaver herself dying just after activating the reactor, which successfully restored power to much of the Los Angeles ruins. The Knights of San Fernando subsequently seized the cold fusion technology and took it with them to [[Area 51]] for their own purposes.Events of {{FOTV|2|2}} It is unclear whether any faction still holds the observatory after this battle. ==In the TV series== ===[[The End (episode)|The End]]=== Griffith Observatory is briefly seen at the start of the episode, as the Great War strikes and nuclear explosions occur in Los Angeles. ===[[The Beginning]]=== By [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], Lucy reaches the walls of the observatory with the cargo of Wilzig's head and is brought to Moldaver, noticing many NCR citizens being sheltered there, including a [[freed ghoul|ghoul she freed]] from the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]] organ harvesters. Upon meeting Moldaver in her headquarters atop the observatory's dome, she attempts to negotiate giving the head and the artifact in exchange for the imprisoned Hank, but Moldaver takes the opportunity to explain the reason why she came to Vault 33 and took her father in the first place, revealing his role in the destruction of Shady Sands including killing thousands of NCR citzens along with turning her mother, [[Rose MacLean|Rose]] into a [[ghoul]]. Lucy's heartbreak over the truth about her father compels Hank to follow Moldaver's orders, inputting his credentials to unlock the cold fusion technology and begin the reactor's power-up.Events of {{FOTV|1|8}} Shortly after, however, the military forces of the Brotherhood arrive and start [[Battle of Griffith Observatory|a battle]] to eradicate the NCR forces and secure control of the reactor. Moldaver attempts to lead her troops in defense of the observatory but the Brotherhood's firepower allows them to plow through the defenders with some casualties. The Ghoul, having also reached the observatory around this time, briefly sets back the Brotherhood's advance when he uses his knowledge of the [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]'s vulnerability to slaughter one of their squads. [[Maximus]] escapes the Ghoul's attack and reaches Lucy and Hank in the control room; he frees Hank but is then incapacitated by him. Hank escapes after being confronted by the Ghoul, and the Ghoul and Lucy leave to track him down. A fatally wounded Moldaver returns to the dome to complete the activation of the cold fusion reactor, dying in her chair while warning Maximus of what could happen if the Brotherhood is allowed to take control of cold fusion. Other Brotherhood forces barge in soon after and celebrate Maximus, assuming he had killed Moldaver. ==Layout== The observatory's outer area has been fortified with junk walls and old car wrecks manned by armed NCR guards to become the stronghold of the Flame Mother, Lee Moldaver. The courtyard is a thriving settlement with families and crop fields with symbols of the NCR adorning the area. The towers of the observatory include anti-air missile launchers that were used during the Brotherhood assault, while some of the guards also wield man-portable rocket-launchers. In the observatory dome, Moldaver maintains the core systems of the cold fusion reactor she is building to restore power to Los Angeles. It also houses a kitchen table where she dines next to the restrained ghoulified husk of Rose MacLean near an exposed ruined wall giving a commanding view of the cityscape ruins. After his capture, Hank MacLean was brought here and kept in a cage until he was needed for Moldaver's plans. ==Appearances== Griffith Observatory appears in the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]] [[Fallout TV series episodes|episodes]] "[[The End (episode)|The End]]" and "[[The Beginning]]." ==Behind the scenes== * The location is based on the real-world [[Wikipedia:Griffith Observatory|Griffith Observatory]] in Los Angeles, California, which opened in 1935. * The practical set of the Griffith Observatory exterior was filmed at the [[wikipedia:Woolworth Estate|Woolworth Estate]] in Long Island, New York, while digital editing was used to create the actual observatory. Some earlier scenes were filmed at the actual Griffith Observatory using second-unit drone footage; these are the only images in season 1 of the TV series that were actually filmed in Southern California. The observatory interior was built at Gold Coast Studios in Long Island, on a [[wikipedia:StageCraft|StageCraft]] soundstage that was specially built for the ''Fallout'' series.[https://archive.ph/A5p5K Los Angeles Times: "In ‘Fallout,’ a destroyed L.A. comes to life, with some help from ... Namibia?"] * The internal scenes of the observatory were created by [[Tony Kwok]], managing and working with an external partner to build the various destroyed set pieces in the environment.[https://www.artstation.com/artwork/rJ6wGL Fallout TV series (Season 1) on Amazon Prime] ==Gallery== Los Angeles Pre-War.png|Griffith Observatory (seen on the left, the domed buildings) during the [[Great War]] Griffith Observatory trailer.png|Griffith Observatory under attack by the Brotherhood of Steel Griffith civilians.png|Civilians inside the settlement FoTV M1918 Browning automatic rifle The Beginning1.jpg|Lucy MacLean escorted by the elite guard FoTV M240C The Beginning1.jpg|Anti-Aircraft emplacements FoTV M1A1 Carbine The Beginning.jpg|Moldaver and her soldiers Hank caged.png|Hank's cage in the shadow of an NCR flag FOTV NCR Poster 1.png|NCR propaganda poster FOTV NCR Poster 2.png|Second propaganda poster ==References== {{References}} '''Meta''' {{References|group=Meta}} {{Navbox Fallout TV series}} [[Category:Fallout TV series locations]] [[ru:Обсерватория Гриффита]]
